Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery Instruments Sectional Committee, MHD 6 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by 
the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. 

This standard is one of the series of vertical Indian Standards on surgical instruments, covering 
only the shape and dimensions of DeBakey type, ring handle, bulldog clamps used in cardiovascular 
surgery. The general requirements and other specification aspects for these clamps are covered in 
IS 3642 (Part 1 ) : 1990 'Specification for surgical instruments : Part 1 Non-cutting, articulated 
type instruments ( second revision )', which is intended to serve as a horizontal standard for these 
clamps. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : I960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values {revised)'. The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value 
in this standard. 



IS 13940 : 1994 



Indian Standard 

CARDIOVASCULAR SURGERY 

INSTRUMENTS — CLAMPS, BULLDOG, 

DeBAKEY, RING HANDLE — SHAPE AND 

DIMENSIONS 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This Indian Standard specifies the shape 
dimensions for Debakey's bulldog clamps 
ring handles used in cardiovascular surgery. 



13.2.2 of Section 3 of IS 3642 



and 
with 



2 REFERENCE 

2.1 IS 3642 (Part I): 1990 'Surgical Instru- 
ments-Non-cutting, articulated type -~ Speci- 
fication {second revisionY forms a necessary 
adjunct to this standard. 

3 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The shape and dimensions of the ring handle 
bulldog clamps shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 

3.2 Jaws 

The clamps shall be provided with straight, curved 
or angled ( 45*, 90"" ) jaws as per the requirement 
of the purchaser. Fig. 1 shows a typical ring 
handle clamp having straight jaws. 

3.3 Joint 

Joint of the instrument shall be box type 



conforming to 
(Part 1) : 1990. 

3.4 Serrations 



3.4.1 The serrations shall be atraugrip ( non- 
traumatic ) with DeBakey type toothing as shown 
in Fig. 1 and shall conform to the relevant 
requirements given in Section 2 of 3642 ( Part 1 ): 
1990. 

3.5 Ratchet 

The ratchet teeth shall be of 1 in 6 combination 
( other combinations also admissible as per requi- 
rement of the purchaser ) and shall satisfy the 
requirements of Section 4 of IS 3642 ( Part 1 ) : 
1990, The load required to perform the load test 
in accordance with 14.2 of IS 3642 ( Part I ) : 
1990 shall be 5N for the first step, I'SN for the 
second step, ION for the third step and so on. 

3.6 Finger Loop 

The finger loops shall conform to Size No. 2 of 
Section 6 of IS 3642 ( Part I ) : 1990. 



IS 13940 : 1994 



ATRAUMATIC SERRATIONS 
(DEBAKEY TYPE) 





All dimensions in millimetres.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, arc 
issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of 
the latest amendments or edition.
